newsitem.title: PERU: Peru Air Force downs drug plane over jungle.
newsitem.headline: Peru Air Force downs drug plane over jungle.

text.p: Peruvian Air Force fighters shot down an airplane suspected of transporting drugs over the central jungle after it ignored instructions to land, news reports on Tuesday said.
The unidentified twin-engined plane crashed after being fired on late on Sunday afternoon near the banks of the Ene River, 200 miles (325 km) east of Lima, according to radio and newspaper reports.
There was no immediate confirmation from Air Force officials in Lima.

The Lima daily El Comercio said the aircraft had just taken off from a clandestine airstrip near the town of Puerto Rico with a cargo of between 800 and 1,000 kg (1,800 and 2,200 lbs) and one metric ton of coca paste when it was spotted by U.S.-operated radar in the town of Pucallpa.
Peru is the world's largest producer of coca, the raw material for making cocaine.
